i.norm: Tests that {@link NodeIterator} supports removing a node during iteration via {@link NodeIterator#remove()}. Removing a node causes its entire subtree to be detached, but the iterator continues visiting any children of the removed node that it had already entered before visiting the remaining siblings.
HTML used by the helper method assertContents; must be set before calling it.
Walks the iterator to completion, appending each node's description to {@code actual}, and asserts that no node is null and that no node is returned twice in a row.
Creates a fresh {@link NodeIterator} rooted at {@code el}, iterates it fully, and asserts the visited sequence matches {@code expected}.
Appends a short human-readable token for {@code node} to {@code actual}: elements are represented as "tag" or "tag#id", text nodes as their text, and all other nodes by their node name.

Verifies the remove-during-iteration contract of {@link NodeIterator}:
  1. When {@link NodeIterator#remove()} is called on a node, the node and its subtree are detached from the document.
  2. The iterator still visits any children of the removed node that it entered before the removal (because the iterator had already descended into that subtree), then continues with the next sibling of the removed node.
  3. Subsequent {@link #assertContents} calls confirm the document reflects the removal.

--- Phase 1: remove div#1 while iterating --- When we encounter div#1 we call remove(). The iterator had already yielded div#1 and will continue into div#2 (and its children) before finishing. div#1's children (p, One, p, Two) are skipped because remove() detaches the subtree before the iterator descends.
div#1 was visited (and removed), its children were not — iterator skipped them.
The document no longer contains div#1 or its children.
--- Phase 2: remove div#2 while iterating the already-modified document ---
div#2 was visited (and removed); its children (p, Three, p, Four) were skipped.
The document now contains neither div#1 nor div#2.
